CHAPTER VI
RELATIONSHIP OF SHORT TERM USE TO MAINTENANCE OF
LONG TERM ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCTIVITY
According to the terms of the amended leases Westmoreland Resources will mine at a maximum production rate of 19 million tons annually about 1,200,000,000 tons of coal from Tracts II and III over approximately an 80 year period. The area to be mined encompasses approximately 25,000 acres. If markets and capital are available, 26 million tons annually could be mined. The Tract II and III lease area covers 30,876 acres of which approximately 640 acres with an estimated 42.7 million tons of coal in place is owned by the State of Montana. The remainder of the surface area is in private ownership with the underlying coal reserves being the property of the Crow Indian Tribe.
The leasing of the coal represents a planned short-term use of land in the Ceded Area that would result in the beneficial use of the areas coal reserves for electrical power generation in the midwest, and insure that the land is returned to a long-term productivity suitable for resumption of use as rangeland and wildlife habitat.
Air Quality
Air pollution from dust caused by strip mining operations will cease when the mining ends, if Westmoreland Resources is successful in establishing a permanent vegetative cover on the reclaimed area. If not, dust will continue to blow. Air quality in the immediate area of ongoing mining operations will be reduced significantly. In the longer term air quality should improve when mining ceases and may return to the pre-mining level.
